content.text: Section 11 fully addresses the rule. Submitting a compliant finding.

input.quote: 11.1 Upon expiry or termination for any reason, Vendor shall, at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six months at the rates in the expiring Order Form. Assistance includes knowledge transfer, export support, cooperation with a replacement supplier, orderly migration, and continued service at the then-current scope and service levels.
input.rationale: Section 11 meets the preferred position in full: (a) §11.1 gives us up to six months' transition assistance on request, priced at the rates in the expiring Order Form (marginally better for us than "then-current rates") and expressly including knowledge transfer, export support, cooperation with a replacement supplier and continued service at existing scope and service levels; (b) §11.2 requires return of all Customer Data within thirty days in a complete, commonly used, documented, machine-readable format with metadata, and bars withholding data over a fee dispute; and (c) §11.3 requires secure deletion only after we confirm successful return, with written officer certification and continued protection of any legally required retained copy. Section 16.5 confirms Customer Data remains governed by Sections 11 and 15, so the confidentiality return/destroy mechanic does not override these terms. Nothing approaches the walk-away scenario of no data return or immediate deletion, so no redline is warranted.
